text.title: Alert-to-Fix Incident Loop Decision Tree
text.summary: Routes on whether an alerting rule actually fired, whether the response fits a solo responder, and whether the page self-resolved inside its own window — to the full loop, a tuning-only pass, or skip.

decision-tree.root-question: Did an alerting rule fire and produce an `alert_id`, or was the incident reported by a customer with no rule behind it?

conclusion.verdict: skip the loop; close the detection gap first — there is no alerting rule for the closing step to patch

branch.question: Does the response need more than one team or vendor, with a separate incident commander and comms lead?

conclusion.verdict: skip; escalate to the coordinated incident-command process — this solo loop has no field for a split response

branch.question: Did the alert fire and self-resolve inside its own evaluation window, with no user-visible impact confirmed?

conclusion.verdict: run the loop in tuning mode only: add a duration hold-down or reformulate as burn-rate, then record the actionability verdict — do not raise the threshold
run the full loop starting from a service-restoring action (rollback, flag off, traffic shift); diagnosis is recorded after mitigation
apply the full loop at non-paging severity: diagnose, fix, patch the rule, file every postmortem action item as an owned ticket
